proposals.evidence: Andersen's āṇapayati cross-reference on printed p. 140 points to the following āṇapay- head, glossed 'to give an order, to command' and compared with Sanskrit ājñāpayati and Pali āṇāpeti. Turner 1096 ājñāpayati explicitly lists Ashokan āñapayāmi, aṇapemi, and ānapayisati.

proposals.evidence: Andersen explicitly glosses the causative pavat- 'to practice [dhammaguna]', compares Sanskrit pra + √vart and Pali pavattati/pavatteti, and prints pavatitaviye/pavatitaviyā. Turner 8788 pravartayati, branch 3, gives Ashokan pavatayevū and pavatitaviyā 'to perform'. This is the verb, distinct from the following pavata- 'mountain'.
